cis_matches.control_title: Restrict RDP exposure and enforce Network Level Authentication
cis_matches.text: Remote Desktop Protocol should not be exposed directly to untrusted networks. Where RDP is required, enforce Network Level Authentication (NLA), require multi-factor authentication, and restrict access via firewall rules or a VPN/bastion host rather than direct internet exposure. Unrestricted RDP exposure is one of the most common initial access vectors in ransomware incidents.

cis_matches.control_title: Disable SMBv1 and require SMB signing
cis_matches.text: Legacy SMBv1 should be disabled on all Windows hosts, as it lacks modern security controls and is the protocol version targeted by well-known remote code execution exploits. SMB signing should be required to prevent relay and tampering attacks. Disable SMBv1 via PowerShell (Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol) or Group Policy, and verify no legacy applications depend on it before rollout.

cis_matches.control_title: Apply security updates for SMB remote code execution vulnerabilities promptly
cis_matches.text: Hosts exposing SMB services should be patched against known remote code execution vulnerabilities as a priority, since SMB is a common lateral-movement and ransomware entry vector. Maintain a patch cadence that applies critical SMB-related security updates within 72 hours of release for internet- or high-value-network-facing systems.
